title: Anthropic Ecosystem and Interfaces
summary: This intermediate module enables learners to evaluate whether the available evidence supports claims about Anthropic's ecosystem and interfaces. Learners can identify unresolved citation problems and determine what must be verified before ecosystem-specific claims are published.
objectives: Identify why a repository-relative path cannot replace a required HTTPS source URL.
Distinguish established information from information that must remain UNKNOWN.
Describe the evidence required to correct the affected content without changing unrelated material.
Recognize why syntactically valid JSON and evidence verification are separate publishing requirements.

sections.title: Level and scope
paragraphs: This is an intermediate module. It assumes that the learner can read structured records and compare a claim with its cited evidence. It does not assume prior knowledge of any specific Anthropic product, interface, model, tool, version, workflow, or configuration key.
The supplied evidence does not establish which products or technical interfaces the existing module covered. Those details are therefore UNKNOWN and are omitted rather than inferred.

sections.title: What changed
paragraphs: The cited source whose condition changed is content/modules/anthropic-claude-practice/anthropic-ecosystem-and-interfaces.json. It was reported as an unregistered publisher record that had never been verified. It is a repository-relative path rather than an HTTPS source URL, so it cannot remain in the corrected sources array under the stated source requirements.
No moved external citation, replacement URL, redirect record, or source-to-claim mapping was supplied. The identity of any external source that moved is therefore UNKNOWN.

The established effect is limited to the evidence trail: the repository-relative citation cannot support publication as an HTTPS source. Its effect on individual ecosystem claims, objectives, explanations, and assessment questions is UNKNOWN because the previous module text was not supplied.
sections.callout: Do not interpret an unavailable baseline as evidence that its claims are false. It means that their support and correction scope cannot yet be verified.

sections.title: How to make an evidence-safe correction
paragraphs: A minimal correction requires the verbatim previous module, its source records, and evidence identifying the replacement for the changed citation. A reviewer must map the changed source to the claims that depend on it, update only those claims and source records, and preserve all unaffected text.

A first-party HTTPS source must be opened and checked before its verification date is recorded. If access, relevance, or the replacement location cannot be confirmed, the corresponding provider-specific claim remains UNKNOWN and must be omitted.

The available evidence does not establish the previous wording, review cadence, estimated time, questions, or source-to-claim relationships. Consequently, preservation of the historical diff cannot be demonstrated from the supplied material alone.

sections.title: JSON validity and evidence validity
paragraphs: ECMA-404 defines JSON as a text syntax containing structured values such as objects and arrays. The ECMAScript specification states that JSON.parse parses JSON text and throws a SyntaxError when the text does not conform to the required grammar.

Successful parsing establishes only that the record is syntactically valid JSON. It does not establish that a citation resolves, that a claim is current, or that an update preserved unaffected material. Those questions require the missing baseline and a successful review of each relevant first-party source.

After completing this module, a learner can separate these two checks: first determine whether the file is valid structured data, then determine whether its subject claims are supported by verified evidence.

sections.title: What remains UNKNOWN
paragraphs: The previous module contents, the external citation alleged to have moved, the replacement source, the affected provider-specific claims, and the prior review cadence are UNKNOWN.

A complete subject-matter correction requires the existing JSON object, its revision history, the review alert or redirect record, the catalogue identifier registry, and successful HTTPS access to every retained or replacement source. Until that evidence is available, no specific Anthropic product, interface, tool, version, configuration key, or workflow can be responsibly introduced.

questions.prompt: What established problem affects the existing cited source?
choices: It is a repository-relative path rather than a required HTTPS source URL.
It documents a confirmed deprecated interface.
It identifies a verified replacement URL.
It proves that every existing ecosystem claim is false.
questions.explanation: The module states that the recorded citation is a repository-relative path from an unregistered publisher and was never verified. No deprecated interface, replacement URL, or false subject claim was established.

questions.prompt: Why is the effect on individual ecosystem claims marked UNKNOWN?
choices: The previous module text and source-to-claim mapping were not supplied.
Repository paths always identify moved external sources.
questions.explanation: Without the previous text and a mapping between its claims and citations, a reviewer cannot determine which claims depended on the changed source.

questions.prompt: Which process best supports a minimal correction?
choices: Infer current products from the module title and rewrite every section.
Delete all citations and retain every claim.
Obtain the previous module, identify claims dependent on the changed source, verify a replacement, and edit only affected material.
Treat successful JSON parsing as proof that every citation is current.
questions.explanation: A minimal correction requires a baseline, a source-to-claim analysis, a verified replacement, and changes limited to the affected material.

questions.prompt: What does successful JSON parsing establish?
choices: The text conforms to JSON syntax.
The update preserved every unaffected sentence.
questions.explanation: Parsing establishes syntactic validity. Source resolution, claim currency, and minimal-diff preservation require separate evidence checks.
